title: The Cipher of the Free Port
premise: Ada Brightwater, a private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed her partner, receives calls on a burner phone from that same dead partner's voice — an AI reconstruction built by a whistleblower hiding inside the Free Port, a lawless offshore trade zone where the world's stolen wealth is laundered. The voice leads Ada to a ledger proving the port's governing consortium ordered the massacre that broke her, but the ledger is also the inheritance her estranged family spent decades burying. As consortium fixers close in and Ada's own employer is revealed to be complicit, she must decide whether to sell the ledger back to the people who want it destroyed or burn it publicly. In the end Ada broadcasts the cipher across the port's own network, sacrificing her career and nearly her life, and walks away with neither justice nor absolution — only the truth, finally spoken aloud.
about_author: Mara Iversen is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent six years auditing cargo manifests out of Rotterdam before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about systems too large to indict and the people small enough to slip through them.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Ada Brightwater, running surveillance on a paranoid client in a rain-soaked harbor district, finds a burner phone sewn into her old field jacket — a jacket she hasn't opened since the incident. When it rings, the voice on the line is her dead partner, Elias. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into impossible hope.

chapters.title: Free Port Rules
chapters.summary: Ada takes a routine contract inside the Free Port, a sovereign-adjacent zone where customs officers take bribes and security firms answer to no court. She uses the access to trace the burner's signal. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: professional competence masking grief; the port feels like a place where the past can be buried forever.

chapters.title: What Elias Left Behind
chapters.summary: The voice explains it is an AI reconstruction trained on Elias's files, activated by a dead-man switch. It claims his death wasn't friendly fire but a sanctioned wipe ordered through the port's consortium. POV: Ada, intercut with a consortium fixer named Voss receiving orders. Emotional beat: rage arriving before proof.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Ada's current client, a disgraced auditor named Renata Kohl, hints she came to the port chasing the same ledger Elias describes. Ada must decide whether Renata is a witness or bait. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: paranoia as survival instinct; trust becomes a tactical decision rather than a feeling.

chapters.title: Warehouse Nine
chapters.summary: Following the voice's coordinates, Ada breaks into Warehouse Nine and finds shredded documents and a cold-storage server rack still humming — someone got there first. Voss's team nearly catches her. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing she's being hunted by professionals who already know her name.

chapters.title: The Incident, Replayed
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: the extraction gone wrong, Elias bleeding out while Ada followed protocol instead of her gut. Present-day Ada realizes the AI voice keeps quoting her own debrief testimony back at her. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: guilt reframed — the incident may have been designed to break her specifically.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Voss corners Ada at a port bar, offering money and erasure of her file if she hands over the phone. He mentions her sister, Juno, by name. POV: alternating Ada and Voss. Emotional beat: fear weaponized; Ada understands the consortium doesn't just want the ledger, it wants leverage over everyone who's seen it.

chapters.title: Juno
chapters.summary: Ada visits her estranged sister, who runs a failing shipping brokerage dependent on port contracts. Juno reveals their late father was one of the Free Port's founding architects — and left them both something sealed. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: the inheritance theme surfaces; family history is not background but the crime scene itself.

chapters.title: The Father's Cipher
chapters.summary: In their father's storage unit, the sisters find a mechanical cipher wheel and a letter admitting he helped design the port's laundering architecture — then tried to build a kill-switch ledger documenting every transaction. The AI voice confirms the ledger still exists, encrypted with the wheel. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; the father's shame becomes the daughters' weapon.

chapters.title: Renata's Ledger
chapters.summary: Renata reveals she audited the consortium for years and has partial keys to the ledger — which is why her predecessor died. She proposes an alliance. That night her hotel room burns. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the cost of proximity to truth; allies are liabilities and Ada knows it, yet can't walk away.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Ada and the Elias-voice work through the night decrypting fragments. The voice begins to falter — its host server is inside the port and Voss is sweeping for it. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: intimacy with a ghost; Ada grieves Elias properly for the first time while racing to save what's left of him.

chapters.title: The Employer's Hand
chapters.summary: Ada discovers her own security firm has been feeding her movements to the consortium since chapter one. Her handler gives her twelve hours to surrender the cipher wheel or be disavowed — meaning no extraction, no legal protection, nothing. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: betrayal closing the last exit; justice outside the law now means outside her own industry too.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: A ticking-clock chapter: Ada moves the wheel through the port's smugglers' tunnels, trading favors with people she once investigated. Every favor costs her a piece of her cover. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grim momentum; the port's underworld proves more honorable than its legitimate face.

chapters.title: Juno's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss pressures Juno with an audit that will bankrupt her firm unless she delivers her sister. Juno instead passes Ada a warning and the second half of their father's key phrase. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: reconciliation without apology; the sisters choose each other over survival.

chapters.title: Server Room Requiem
chapters.summary: Ada reaches the AI's host server in the port's data vault just as Voss's team begins physically destroying racks. She saves a fragment drive containing the Elias model and half the decrypted ledger. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: losing the ghost twice; the voice says goodbye mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: With half a ledger, Ada can prove nothing — and the consortium knows it. Renata, presumed dead, resurfaces with the missing decryption keys hidden in an insurance filing. POV: Renata. Emotional beat: cautious rekindled trust; three damaged women form an unlikely tribunal.

chapters.title: The Consortium Meets
chapters.summary: Ada infiltrates the consortium's annual reconciliation dinner using Renata's credentials, watching the men who ordered the massacre toast each other. She copies the final ledger keys from a terminal in plain sight. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: cold fury; seeing impunity up close converts grief into resolve.

chapters.title: Caught Between
chapters.summary: Voss intercepts Ada at the docks. He offers the deal again — full erasure, Juno protected, the incident officially rewritten as heroism — if she surrenders everything. For one long beat, she wants it. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable lies; the chapter ends with Ada choosing the hard truth and taking a bullet graze escaping.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: from the port's central transmission tower, Ada, Renata, and Juno broadcast the complete ledger across every screen and speaker in the Free Port during the consortium's flagship auction. Chaos erupts; buyers flee, ships scatter, Voss's team storms the tower. POV: rotating among the three women. Emotional beat: catharsis under fire; the truth costs blood but lands.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Rain
chapters.summary: Voss is arrested by port authorities scrambling to salvage legitimacy — a scapegoat, and Ada knows it. The consortium's deeper structures survive. Ada deletes the Elias fragment herself, refusing to let him become evidence. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: bitter victory; justice outside the law is partial, temporary, human.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the sisters settle their father's estate: the cipher wheel, formally worthless now, and a letter he wrote assuming they'd never read it. Juno rebuilds her brokerage clean. Ada declines three job offers from firms wanting to weaponize what she knows. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning; memory honored rather than monetized.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: On a ferry leaving the port behind, Ada sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident — no dreams of Elias, no ringing phones. A stranger asks what she does for a living. 'Nothing anyone needs guarding,' she says. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: earned peace, provisional and unsentimental; the arc closes on rest, not resolution.
